subject: MSstatsTMT missing value imputation bug: extreme logFC > 70

messages.author: b4f45db4340c181c
messages.subject: MSstatsTMT missing value imputation bug: extreme logFC > 70
parts:
Hi all,

We observed extreme log2 fold changes in control vs treatment contrasts. Tracking this down, it seems this is due to missing value imputation.

Please see image below, showing PSMs input to MSstatsTMT as well as MSstatsTMT feature output with imputed values:


While it's clear to me that a small number e.g. 2.8e-42 will result in -138 in log2 space. What I'm questioning is if this is a reasonable value and assumption for TMT abundances.
Shouldn't there be a minimum value e.g. 1 in log2 space for imputed values? This would be in order for extreme log2 ratios (numerator vs denominator condition) can't happen.

We're using Proteome Discoverer PSMs files of TMT16plex as input, and processed using MSstatsTMT version 2.8.0.

Thank you for all your efforts!!

Best,
David

messages.subject: Re: MSstatsTMT missing value imputation bug: extreme logFC > 70
parts:
Apologies for the delay in my response!

I've tested the following inputs
A.) keep only PSMs for protein in question
B.) randomly sample 2000 PSMs plus the PSMs for the protein in question
C.) the entirety of PSMs, meaning the original data frame
The protein in question is called "ABC123" (anonymized), I have seen similar issues in other experiments (these are 16 or 18plex TMT experiments of human cell lines with DMSO as control and small molecule treatments). 

A and B resulted in reasonable log2FC, i.e. small changes around 0. Only C resulted in log2FC < 145 (see "output_running_r_script.txt"). Result C is reproducible. 

Software version:
MSstatsTMT version 2.8.0
MSstats version 4.10.0
Also tried it with MSstatsTMT version 2.10.0, getting the same results.

I've attached the R script to reproduce the results, the input files for "A" and "B" (see above), as well as the output, highlighting the difference of dramatic log2FC (see below).
I hope this helps. Let me know should you need other info/data. I would be happy and grateful to know where the issue lies. Please keep me posted.

Many thanks for all your efforts !!

Best,
David

messages.author: b4f45db4340c181c
messages.subject: Re: MSstatsTMT missing value imputation bug: extreme logFC > 70
parts:
Hi Mateusz / MSstats-users,

thank you so much for investigating the issue!!

In our pipeline I've implemented the following logic to circumvent the problem of exorbitant log-fold-changes due to imputation: for features of a protein check if any imputed value is higher/lower than the max/min of non-imputed features of that protein. If this is the case, then do not impute the values for any feature of that protein.

It would be great if a future release of MSstats(TMT) would have a solution for the issue. I'd expect this to lead to fewer missing values than my work-around.

Thank you for all your time and effort !!

Best,
David
